pr.title: Let a person send the agent a message about an item, a pull request, or the session
pr.head: 748b0b8430cfe972f3acacc6f7cf537c61379dbe

summary: Projector’s inbox holds the questions, notices, and requests an agent posts for you. This layer lets you send the agent a message about one of those items, a pull request, or the session without typing into its chat.

Messages travel one way. Your words reach the owning session as DISCUSS lines; the agent answers in its own conversation. An item keeps the messages you sent about it, while a standalone message item resolves itself once its pending messages finish.

The inbox remains a list of what needs you rather than a second conversation. The terminal console and its session-conversation view belong to later layers. This layer supplies storage, commands, panel display, and permission rules.

cards.title: One message is in flight per item
cards.html: A claim holds one line for one deliverer. A DISCUSS claim records the message index, so a later message cannot change which one is settled. Answers and existing lifecycle lines are sent before unclaimed messages.

cards.title: Full review of the revised design
cards.html: Gate and exact-head CI passed, including 243 hook tests, plus 217 focused Python tests. Removing standalone message auto-resolution makes its lifecycle test fail. No new findings or suggestions remain.

groups.title: Record and deliver your messages
groups.kicker: Keep message order and resolve standalone sends
intro: You can attach messages to an open inbox item, or send a standalone message about a pull request or the session. Each message is one paragraph of at most 4 KiB in UTF-8. The existing item store provides locked, atomic writes.

A deliverer claims the oldest owed message, sends its DISCUSS line, and settles that message by index. Messages stay owed after an answer or dismissal. A standalone message item resolves after its last message is delivered or taken back, so it leaves no empty open item.

files.note: Adds one-way messages, the message item kind, entry-specific delivery, and standalone-item resolution.

checks.text: The focused tests passed for ordered delivery, held claims, failed delivery, dismissal survival, command refusals, and byte limits. Omitting automatic resolution makes the standalone message lifecycle test fail.

files.note: Exposes discuss for all three targets, prints sent messages, and wakes Codex delivery.

groups.title: Show sent messages without duplicating chat
groups.kicker: Keep replies in the agent’s conversation
intro: Claude Code’s panel lists standalone message items and shows the messages you sent under you: in each drawer. A line reads sending while it owes a message. Delivery uses the panel’s existing claims and prompt submission.

A message item asks nothing of you, so it has no answer choices or clarification control and leaves the panel after delivery. Agent reply tools and unread-reply tracking are absent: the agent answers in its conversation.

checks.text: All 243 hook tests passed, covering ordered discussion delivery, failed sends, sending status, message display and controls, and delivered-item departure.

files.note: Defines sent-message records and the message item union member.
Recognizes owed messages while keeping answers scoped to questions and requests.
Displays your messages, message-item controls, and pending delivery; no reply/read machinery remains.

groups.title: Preserve the person’s authority
intro: Writing a discussion message speaks as you. It therefore requires the same approval boundary as answering an item, so an agent cannot put words in your mouth.

The shared instructions tell an agent to answer DISCUSS in its conversation, then revise, withdraw, or leave an existing item open as appropriate. A message about a pull request or the session needs no inbox action.

checks.text: Permission, packaging, and instruction tests passed for the discuss approval decision, removed reply/read commands, and template version 31.

files.note: Asks before discuss and carries no reply/read permission surface.
Updates the shared instructions for conversation replies and advances the template version.
Tells unattended agents how to respond to discussion lines.

groups.title: Document the one-way contract
groups.kicker: Keep commands, panel behavior, and the active plan aligned
intro: The CLI reference explains the three discussion targets, message limits, delivery order, and failure behavior. The plugin guide describes the panel’s sent-message display.

The active console plan now keeps replies in the session conversation and records why per-item threads were rejected. Later layers build the multi-session console and conversation view; this layer provides the messaging foundation.
